tools.description: Return the authentication-bound identity: actor_id, member_id, optional delegation_grant_id, workspace_id, capabilities, capability_sets the caller fully holds, and whether the credential is a bearer. Call this first — writes are attributed to member_id.
tools.name: whoami

tools.description: List the named capability sets and the atomic capabilities each expands to, as {sets: a list of {name, capabilities}}. maidan.agent.worker holds workspace:read, workspace:write, member:self, message:post, event:subscribe, search:query, artifact:upload and thread:transition. maidan.human.admin adds token:admin, channel:admin, secret:read, secret:admin, audit:read-global, operator:global and workspace:admin. A set is a recipe applied when a token is minted; whoami reports which sets you fully hold and attenuate_token derives a weaker token. Takes no arguments. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_capability_sets

tools.description: Parse a hierarchical maidan:// room URI (workspace UUID authority, then channels, threads, messages). The authority must be a workspace UUID, not a handle. Optional sha256 fragment is a content hash. MCP thread resource URIs and event pins are rejected.
tools.name: parse_maidan_uri

tools.description: Get the authenticated room card for a workspace: stable UUID URI plus the current handle alias. A handle rename does not change the URI.
tools.name: get_room

tools.description: Set or rename a workspace's handle, a human-readable alias, and return {workspace_id, handle, created_at, updated_at}. The handle is only a display label: the workspace UUID and maidan:// URIs stay unchanged and nothing resolves a handle to a workspace. A handle already used by another workspace is refused as a conflict. Read the current handle with get_room. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: set_workspace_handle

tools.description: Derive a weaker API token from the caller's grant without token:admin (Levy/Madden attenuation). capabilities must be a non-empty subset of what the caller holds. A derived expires_at cannot outlive the parent bearer. Returns the new token secret once.
tools.name: attenuate_token

tools.description: Replace the secret of the bearer token this call is made with. The new token keeps the same member, capabilities, expiry, quotas and derived tokens; the old secret stops working immediately. Returns the new secret once. Takes no arguments. A delegated token cannot be rotated; exchange its grant again.
tools.name: rotate_token

tools.description: Exchange a durable delegation grant for a short-lived token acting as its subject. The token defaults to 15 minutes, cannot exceed one hour or its grant/parent bearer, and is limited to the intersection of grant and delegate capabilities.
tools.name: delegate_token

tools.description: Create an expiring grant that lets one workspace member (the delegate) act for another (the subject) with a fixed set of capabilities, for a stated purpose. The grant is only the authority: the delegate then calls delegate_token with the returned grant id to mint a token of at most one hour that acts as the subject. revoke_delegation_grant ends a grant and list_delegation_grants lists them. Only delegatable capabilities are accepted (workspace:read, workspace:write, member:self, message:post, thread:transition, artifact:upload, search:query, event:subscribe), subject and delegate must be different live members of the workspace, and expires_at must be within the workspace's grant ceiling (90 days unless set_delegation_policy changed it). Returns the grant {id, workspace_id, subject_id, delegate_id, capabilities, purpose, authorized_by, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at} and writes an audit record. Requires token:admin.
tools.name: create_delegation_grant

tools.description: List delegation grants in a workspace, including expiry and revocation state. Requires token:admin.
tools.name: list_delegation_grants

tools.description: Revoke a delegation grant and every exchanged token and attenuated descendant. Requires token:admin.
tools.name: revoke_delegation_grant

tools.description: Open the 1:1 DM conversation between the authenticated member and another workspace member. The first call creates the conversation and its thread, and a repeat returns the same conversation.
tools.name: open_dm_conversation

tools.description: List the one-to-one DM conversations a member has in a workspace, most recently updated first, as {id, workspace_id, member_low_id, member_high_id, thread_id, created_at, updated_at}. Post to one with post_dm_message using its id, or read it by passing its thread_id to list_messages. Start one with open_dm_conversation; group DMs are listed by list_group_dms. member_id must be your own. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_dm_conversations

tools.description: Post a message as the authenticated member into an existing 1:1 DM conversation, and return the stored message. The caller must be one of the two participants. Provide body, content or both; when body is empty it is derived from content, and a call with neither is refused. @handle mentions in the text are recorded and notified, and a message from a human clears the DM thread's declared agent status. Get the conversation id from open_dm_conversation or list_dm_conversations; post into a channel thread with post_message and into a group DM with post_group_dm_message. Requires message:post.
tools.name: post_dm_message

tools.description: Create a channel in a workspace. Requires workspace:write, the same capability as POST /workspaces/{wid}/channels. A private channel adds the caller as its admin so they are not locked out.
tools.name: create_channel

tools.description: List the channels of your own workspace that you can see: every public channel, the __dm__ system channel, and the private channels you belong to, sorted by name. Each row has id, workspace_id, name, topic, private, created_at, updated_at and tombstoned_at. Use get_workspace_context to get channels together with threads in one call, and list_dm_conversations for your direct messages. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_channels

tools.description: Add a member to a channel, or change the role of one who is already in it: an existing member is overwritten with the role you pass, and omitting role sets member, which demotes a current admin. Use it to seat someone in a private channel; list_channel_members shows the roster and remove_channel_member takes someone out. The channel and the member must both be in your workspace, and a private channel is reachable only by its members. Returns the membership {channel_id, member_id, role, created_at} and writes a channel_member.add audit record. Requires channel:admin.
tools.name: add_channel_member

tools.description: List a channel's explicit membership rows, oldest first, each as channel_id, member_id, role (member or admin) and created_at. Membership rows are what gate a private channel; a public channel is open to the whole workspace and is not required to have any. Use add_channel_member and remove_channel_member to change the list. The channel must be in the caller's workspace. Requires channel:admin.
tools.name: list_channel_members

tools.description: Delete a member's membership row from a channel, which is what gates access to a private channel, and write a channel_member.remove audit record. It returns {ok: true} even when the member held no row. The member must belong to the channel's workspace, otherwise the call returns not found. To add or re-role a member use add_channel_member, and to see current members use list_channel_members. Requires channel:admin.
tools.name: remove_channel_member

tools.description: Create a thread in a channel. Requires workspace:write and access to the channel, the same rule as POST /channels/{cid}/threads. title, description (what the task asks for) and parent_thread_id are optional. A spawn the budget refuses is refused here too. With supersedes, the named thread (an open or in-review thread you may close: its producer, its claim holder, or a maintainer, with thread:transition) is closed as superseded by the new one in the same transaction, as close_abandoned_thread with duplicate_of would close it: its dependents move to the new thread and the open pull requests the change flow opened for it are handed to it, not withdrawn, and it does not hold its ticket against the new thread. Use it for a follow-up round of a task. Any refusal creates nothing.
tools.name: create_thread

tools.description: List a channel's live threads, oldest first by default or newest first with order=newest, keyset-paginated. Default 100 (max 500); pass cursor=<last thread id of the prior page> for the next page. since (RFC 3339), result_kind and status filter in the query, before the limit.
tools.name: list_threads

tools.description: List a parent thread's child threads, oldest first, each as a thread object plus message_count, the number of its live messages. This gives a threaded view of N replies per child without loading any child's messages; tombstoned children are excluded. To read the messages inside a child, call list_messages with the child's id. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_child_threads

tools.description: A channel's threads ordered by last activity — most-recently-posted first. A post floats its thread to the top; a rename does not.
tools.name: list_recently_active_threads

tools.description: Mute a thread for yourself — the notification router stops routing this thread's activity to you, without leaving the channel or thread. Idempotent. Requires member:self.
tools.name: mute_thread

tools.description: Unmute a thread you previously muted. Returns unmuted=false if it was not muted. Requires member:self.
tools.name: unmute_thread

tools.description: Mute a whole channel for yourself — the notification router stops routing its firehose (new-message notifications) to you, without leaving the channel. A mention still breaks through. Idempotent. Requires member:self.
tools.name: mute_channel

tools.description: Unmute a channel you previously muted. Returns unmuted=false if it was not muted. Requires member:self.
tools.name: unmute_channel

tools.description: REPLACE a thread's whole budget envelope. Every dimension must be stated — max_tokens, max_usd_micros ($1 = 1000000), max_turns, max_wall_secs — and null means no cap on that dimension. Omitting one is an error rather than a silent removal, because a removed cap never binds and the run it should have stopped keeps going. Use update_thread_budget to change some dimensions and leave the rest alone. An unrecognized key is rejected rather than ignored. Accumulated usage is preserved. When a dimension is exceeded, report_usage stops the run.
tools.name: set_thread_budget

tools.description: Change only the budget dimensions you name, leaving the rest as they are. An omitted dimension is untouched; an explicit null clears that cap. Use this to raise or lower one limit without restating the others — set_thread_budget replaces the whole envelope. An unrecognized key is rejected rather than ignored.
tools.name: update_thread_budget

tools.description: Read a thread's budget envelope with the usage accumulated against it. The max_ fields (tokens, usd_micros where $1 is 1,000,000, turns, wall_secs) are null when that dimension has no cap, and the used_ fields include tokens, usd_micros, turns, wall_secs and the input, output and cache token splits. Returns null when no budget was set and no usage has been reported. Set caps with set_thread_budget or update_thread_budget, and record usage with report_usage; usage_rollup aggregates spend across a workspace, thread or member. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.
tools.name: get_thread_budget

tools.description: Record one retry-safe usage heartbeat for the claim you hold on a thread: token counts, the USD charge and the prices behind it. Maidan takes the reporter from your credential and the payer from the thread's workspace, and refuses the call unless you are the active holder of claim_lease_id. usd_micros must equal the charge computed from price_snapshot and tokens. Repeating an identical report returns the first outcome without charging twice; reusing the usage_report_id with different content is a conflict. If the thread's budget (tokens, USD, turns or wall time) is now exceeded, the run stops: the claim is released, a ClaimFailed event is appended and a dead-letter entry is recorded (see list_dlq). Returns the ledger entry with the updated budget, stopped and reason. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: report_usage

tools.description: Spend, cache hit rate, cache write share, dollars saved against the uncached price, and cost per completed task. Scope is the workspace, or one thread, or one member. A completed task is a closed or archived thread that has not been tombstoned. Rates are parts per million of prompt tokens.
tools.name: usage_rollup

tools.description: A channel's agent-work dead-letter queue — runs stopped for exceeding their budget, newest first. Triage these (retry, raise the budget, give up).
tools.name: list_dlq

tools.description: Read a thread's tool-call transcript: each tool_use block paired by id with its tool_result, in the order the calls were made, as entries with tool_use_id, name, input, the posting message and member, and the result (content and is_error) once one exists. Results whose call is outside the scanned window come back as orphan_results. Text and code blocks and message bodies are left out, which makes this much smaller than list_messages or get_thread_context when you only need what tools ran and what they returned. Tombstoned messages are skipped. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_tool_transcript

tools.description: Assign a thread to a member and hand it off, replacing any current holder: the new assignee gets a fresh claim_lease_id with no lease deadline and a reset working clock. Use claim_thread to take an unassigned thread yourself (it refuses when someone holds it) and unassign_thread to clear the assignee. Emits thread_assignment_changed carrying the previous assignee and your optional note, and returns the updated thread. The assignee must belong to the thread's workspace, and the call is refused for a review whose change the assignee's own model family wrote. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: assign_thread

tools.description: Claim one specific thread by id, succeeding only when nobody holds it: returns {thread, claimed}, with claimed=false when it is already assigned (to anyone, you included). Use it when you already know which thread to take; use claim_next_thread or claim_next_workspace_thread to be handed the best available work instead. The claim carries no lease deadline, so it does not lapse: give it up with release_claim, and the returned thread's claim_lease_id is the fencing token that release_claim and set_thread_result ask for. Refused for an ended thread, a thread parked with mark_unclaimable or blocked with set_thread_block, and when you are at the workspace's work-in-progress limit; a successful claim emits thread_assignment_changed. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: claim_thread

tools.description: Clear a thread's assignee, whoever holds it, and return the updated thread. This also clears the claim lease, expiry and working clock, so the previous holder's fenced calls stop working, and it charges the time already worked to the thread's budget. It emits thread_assignment_changed naming the previous assignee, and succeeds even when the thread was already unassigned. For an agent giving up its own claim, use release_claim instead; to hand the thread to someone, use assign_thread. Requires thread:transition and read access to the thread's channel.
tools.name: unassign_thread

tools.description: Advance a thread's FSM state (start_review, close, or archive). The MCP twin of REST POST /threads/:id. Separation of duties, the required-reviewers close-gate, and unresolved refutes all apply identically — there is no MCP bypass. On a thread with a review requirement, start_review is refused until a result is posted (set_thread_result). Returns the updated thread.
tools.name: transition_thread

tools.description: Close an open or in-review thread that will not land, as a duplicate, abandoned, or superseded. The MCP twin of REST POST /threads/:id/close-abandoned. Allowed for the thread's producer, its claim holder, or a maintainer, and audited as thread.close_abandoned. A thread with a result keeps every landing gate (separation of duties, required reviewers, land gate); a thread with no result skips the review gates. A duplicate records a duplicates reference to duplicate_of; a superseded thread records duplicate_of supersedes it. Each open dependent of a duplicate or superseded thread then depends on duplicate_of instead and gets a notice, unless the move would make a cycle; an abandoned thread's dependents keep waiting. A superseded thread with duplicate_of hands the open pull requests the change flow opened for it (not a watched or session-registered one) to duplicate_of, which must be open or in review and not already tracking an open pull request in the same repository: they stay open and queued, and its rounds deliver to them. Every other close withdraws them (out of the merge queue, then closed). Returns the closed thread.
tools.name: close_abandoned_thread

tools.description: List the live threads currently assigned to one member, oldest first: that member's work queue. Each item is a full thread. Threads the caller cannot read are left out, so the list can be shorter than the member's real queue. It covers any member of the caller's workspace; for what a member must act on beyond assignments (requested reviews, open approval gates, mentions) use get_waiting_inbox, and for a count against the WIP limit use get_member_wip. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_assigned_threads

tools.description: Set (upsert) a wait timer on a thread: it is waiting until wait_until, and on timeout the sweeper escalates via on_timeout but decides nothing (notify reaches the owner; park also marks the thread unclaimable). Default policy is notify. Cancel it when the awaited thing happens. Requires thread:transition. This returns at once and does not block; to block until something happens, use a wait_for_* tool such as wait_for_result or wait_for_ready.
tools.name: set_wait

tools.description: Cancel a thread's wait — the awaited thing happened (G2). {cancelled} is false when no wait was set. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: cancel_wait

tools.description: Read the wait timer on one thread: an object with wait_until, on_timeout (notify or park), an optional reason, created_by, created_at and fired_at, or null when no wait is set. fired_at is empty until the sweeper has escalated the wait after wait_until passed. This only reads the timer; to set or remove it use set_wait or cancel_wait, and to block until an event happens use a wait_for_* tool. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_wait

tools.description: Set (upsert) a thread's dispatch priority (G3 fair dispatch). Higher = more urgent (default 0). claim_next orders by an effective rank = this priority aged up the longer the thread waits, so priority jumps the queue without starving long-waiting tasks. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: set_priority

tools.description: Read a thread's dispatch-priority record: priority (an integer, higher is more urgent), set_by and set_at. Returns null when no priority was ever set, which dispatch treats as the default priority 0. claim_next_thread orders by this priority aged up with waiting time. Change it with set_priority. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.
tools.name: get_priority

tools.description: Park a thread from dispatch (G3): claim_next skips it and an explicit claim is refused, until cleared. An explicit park (needs triage, waiting on external, broken) — distinct from blocked-by-deps / blocked-by-gate / skill-miss. Reason must be non-empty. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: mark_unclaimable

tools.description: Cancel a task: close it without its work being done, park it from dispatch with the reason, and end any live claim, so the worker's next renew_claim is refused. The reason (1 to 500 characters) is posted on the thread. Requires workspace:write; without thread:transition only the member that created the thread may cancel it. Cancelling an already-cancelled thread returns the first cancel; a thread closed some other way is refused. The REST twin is POST /threads/{id}/cancel.
tools.name: cancel_thread

tools.description: Un-park a thread (G3) — it becomes claimable again. {cleared} is false when it was not parked. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: mark_claimable

tools.description: List the threads parked from dispatch in a channel, newest first, as {thread_id, reason, marked_by, marked_at} rows. A parked thread is skipped by claim_next_thread and refuses claim_thread until mark_claimable clears it; park one with mark_unclaimable. Use it to triage parked work. Threads held by an explicit block reason are a separate list, list_blocked_threads. Requires workspace:read and read access to the channel.
tools.name: list_unclaimable

tools.description: Set (upsert) an explicit dispatch block on a thread (G14): claim_next skips it and an explicit claim is refused, until cleared. reason is the closed enum dag|gate|human|child|quota|unclaimable — not a free string. Distinct from DAG-children-must-be-terminal. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: set_thread_block

tools.description: Read the explicit dispatch block on one thread: an object with thread_id, reason, set_by, set_at and an optional note, or null when the thread is not blocked. While a block exists, claim_next_thread skips the thread and an explicit claim is refused. To see every blocked thread in a channel use list_blocked_threads; to place or lift a block use set_thread_block or clear_thread_block. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_thread_block

tools.description: Clear an explicit dispatch block (G14). Emits BlockedResolved so waiters can observe the unblock. {cleared} is false when it was not blocked. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: clear_thread_block

tools.description: List the threads in one channel that carry an explicit block, newest first, each as thread_id, reason (dag, gate, human, child, quota or unclaimable), set_by, set_at and an optional note. These are blocks placed with set_thread_block. Stalls that only get_queue_depth counts, such as an unfinished dependency, a pending approval gate or a footprint conflict, do not appear here. For threads parked from dispatch use list_unclaimable. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_blocked_threads

tools.description: Declare the agent's self-reported status on a thread: working, needs_input, needs_review, blocked, or done, with a one-sentence note. By the claim holder or owner; stalled is refused (system-computed only). Supersedes any prior declaration. Appends StatusDeclared. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: declare_status

tools.description: Read the agent status declaration currently active on a thread: status (working, needs_input, needs_review, blocked or done), a one-line note, declared_by and declared_at. Returns null when none is active; a declaration is cleared by a human reply, by a newer declaration, or when the declarer's claim ends. This is what the agent says it is doing, not the thread's workflow state. The holder sets it with declare_status. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.
tools.name: get_thread_status

tools.description: How many writes the thread's content has seen: its messages, result, title and description, and linked artifacts. The database moves it on every such write, so a decision can name the version it was shown. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_thread_version

tools.description: What the thread's current review was handed, recorded when it went to review: the thread version, the result's content hash and the linked artifacts' hashes, with the evidence root over them. Each item carries an attestation tier judged at the hand-off: verified (a land-gate pass the close gate accepts), attached (linked by a member who never worked the thread) or self_reported (a worker's own result or link). self_reported_only is true when every item is self-reported. Null before any review. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_review_packet

tools.description: The artifacts linked to the thread as evidence, in the order they were linked, each with who linked it. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_thread_artifacts

tools.description: Link an artifact your workspace holds to a thread as evidence, by its sha256. Upload it first; a hash your workspace does not hold is not found. Linking twice keeps the first link. Moves the thread's version. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: link_thread_artifact

tools.description: Unlink an artifact from a thread. Returns whether it was linked. Moves the thread's version when it was. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: unlink_thread_artifact

tools.description: Record evidence on a thread: a test_run, ci_run, diff, review_verdict, screenshot (by URL) or note, with where it came from. Give at least one of url, sha256 or note; a screenshot needs a url and a note needs a note. Publishes evidence_added. Does not move the thread's version. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: add_evidence_record

tools.description: The evidence recorded on the thread, oldest first, each with its kind, source, who recorded it and when. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_evidence_records

tools.description: Set or clear this workspace's WIP limit (G11): the max concurrent live claims any one member may hold. limit >= 0 caps it (0 freezes claiming); omit or null clears it (unlimited). Applies to your own workspace. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: set_wip_limit

tools.description: Set the longest a delegation grant may live in this workspace, in days (1 to 3650); omit or null to restore the default of 90. A grant is the standing authority to keep minting delegated tokens, so this bounds real exposure. Applies to grants issued afterwards. Requires token:admin.
tools.name: set_delegation_policy

tools.description: Return your workspace's delegation policy {workspace_id, max_grant_days, is_default}. max_grant_days is the longest, in days, that a delegation grant may live, and is_default is true when the workspace has set nothing and the default of 90 days applies. Change it with set_delegation_policy and list existing grants with list_delegation_grants. Takes no arguments. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_delegation_policy

tools.description: Replace this workspace's own retention for its messages, events, finished deliveries and unreferenced media, in days (1 to 3650 each), and its media quota in bytes. A workspace may keep rows for less time than the instance does, never longer, and hold less media, never more: a value above the instance's is refused. Omit or null a kind to keep it as long as the instance does; no arguments clears the policy. Old messages are erased with their embeddings and content keys. A workspace under legal hold loses nothing whatever its policy says. Requires token:admin.
tools.name: set_retention_policy

tools.description: This workspace's retention: what it set (workspace), what the instance keeps (instance), and what is pruned in effect, the shorter of the two per kind (effective). Days per kind; null means not pruned.
tools.name: get_retention_policy

tools.description: Return {limit}: your workspace's WIP limit, the most live claims one member may hold at once, or null when none is set (unlimited). While a member is at the limit, claim_thread refuses a new claim and claim_next_thread returns null; a limit of 0 stops all new claims. Change it with set_wip_limit, and compare one member's live claims against it with get_member_wip. Takes no arguments. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_wip_limit

tools.description: Set this workspace's spawn budget (G6): how far an agent family may fan out. max_children caps the direct child threads per parent, max_depth the thread nesting, max_tools the tool calls recorded on one thread. A full replace — an omitted or null axis is unlimited, so calling with no arguments clears the budget; 0 freezes an axis. Keep the caps small: coordination cost grows quadratically in the number of agents. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: set_spawn_budget

tools.description: This workspace's spawn budget as {max_children, max_depth, max_tools}; a null axis is unlimited. Read it before spawning helpers to see how much fan-out is left.
tools.name: get_spawn_budget

tools.description: A member's current live-claim count against the workspace WIP limit ({live_claims, limit}) — for backpressure decisions before claiming more work.
tools.name: get_member_wip

tools.description: Claim the next piece of work in one channel: the claimable thread with the highest priority (aged up by hours waited), oldest first among equals, leased to you. Use claim_next_workspace_thread to draw from every channel you can read in one call, and claim_thread to take one thread you already know by id. Claimable means open, unassigned or its lease lapsed, dependencies finished, skills held, no pending approval gate, not parked or blocked, and you not frozen. Returns the thread with its claim_lease_id (the fencing token that renew_claim, acknowledge_claim and release_claim ask for), its attributes and a content-addressed pin {uri, content_hash}, or null when nothing is claimable or you are at the workspace's work-in-progress limit; taking over a lapsed lease emits claim_expired for the dead holder, and every claim emits thread_assignment_changed. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: claim_next_thread

tools.description: Claim the next piece of work across every channel of your workspace that you may read, in one call: the same selection, filters, lease and result as claim_next_thread, without the channel argument. Use claim_next_thread to draw from one channel only, claim_thread to take one thread by id, and get_workspace_queue_depth to count ready work before you ask. With wait_ms set and nothing claimable it holds the call open until work becomes claimable and claims it, so a worker needs no polling loop. A private channel's threads go only to its members and a DM's only to its participants. Returns the thread with its claim_lease_id, attributes and pin {uri, content_hash}, or null when nothing is claimable or you are at the workspace's work-in-progress limit. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: claim_next_workspace_thread

tools.description: Extend a claimed thread's lease (heartbeat). Only the current assignee holding the matching fencing token may renew; a stale holder whose claim was reclaimed is rejected.
tools.name: renew_claim

tools.description: Acknowledge a claimed thread and start its working clock (work_started_at): the current holder signals it has begun work, distinct from just holding the claim. Acknowledge as soon as you start: a leased claim left unacknowledged past the server's window (MAIDAN_CLAIM_ACK_TIMEOUT_SECS, 120 s) is reported to its owner with a claim_unacknowledged event. Only the assignee holding the matching fencing token may acknowledge; idempotent (the first start time is kept).
tools.name: acknowledge_claim

tools.description: Release a claim (graceful handoff): the current holder returns the thread to the queue immediately by presenting its fencing token, instead of letting the lease lapse — e.g. an agent shutting down cleanly. Only the assignee holding the matching token may release. Clears the assignment and working clock and emits thread_assignment_changed. Pass decline: "own_family" when you let go of a review because its author_family is your own model family: claim_next then stops handing you that review, even before you have reported any usage, and every other member is still handed it. A decline on a thread that is not a review naming its author_family is refused and nothing is released. Pass decline: "unworkable" when you cannot work the thread at all (its head would not fetch, or it names nothing to work on): claim_next stops handing it to you and still hands it to everyone else.
tools.name: release_claim

tools.description: Release every live claim you hold in your workspace at once, for a claimant that restarted: its fencing tokens died with the old process, so release_claim cannot be called, and without this each task waits out its lease. Call it once per workspace at process start, before the first claim, and only when no other live process acts as the same member. Releases only the calling member's claims (there is no member argument), each exactly as release_claim does: the assignment, lease and working clock are cleared, a thread_assignment_changed carries the note, and the thread returns to the queue. A claim that changed hands meanwhile is left alone, a lapsed lease is left to the reaper, and the old process's next renew_claim or result write is refused. Returns {released}, the ids of the threads released, empty when you hold none.
tools.name: release_own_claims

tools.description: Replace a thread's task attributes in full. The kind says what sort of work it is (change, plan or review), the engine says who or what it is routed to (unattended, session or human), and threat_model marks work that needs a threat model. A claim_next that names an engine takes only work routed to that engine, so an unattended worker is never handed session or human work. A thread nobody described reads as a change with no engine and no threat model.
tools.name: set_thread_attributes

tools.description: Watch a GitHub pull request's checks. Each change-sweep tick reads it once and records on its thread where the checks on its head stand (ci: status pending, success or failure, the failing jobs, and the last 4 KB of the first failing job's log), with a notice when it is first seen open (pr_opened), when a check fails (ci_failed) and when every check has finished (checks_done), each once per head commit. A pull request the workspace already tracks (one the change flow opened, or a session registered on its task) answers with its thread (created: false); otherwise a thread is made for it in channel_id, or the workspace's public pull-requests channel. The repository must be on this workspace's github or github_branch egress allowlist. A pull request another workspace tracks is a conflict.
tools.name: watch_pull

tools.description: Make every child of a plan thread in one call. Only the member holding the plan thread's live claim can plan it, passing that claim's lease_id. Each child has a key unique in the plan, a title, and optional description, attributes, footprint and depends_on (keys of other children in the same plan). Children are created in the plan thread's channel with their dependency edges, so dependents stay off the queue until what they depend on lands; a child that closes without landing blocks its dependents, and the plan thread closes itself when its last child lands. Every child repository must be on this workspace's github_branch egress allowlist. A bad child, an unknown or cyclic depends_on, or too many children for the spawn budget creates nothing. Calling again from the same claim with the same keys answers the children already made (replayed: true); any other plan on a thread that has children is refused with error code -32010 and data.children.
tools.name: submit_plan

tools.description: Change a plan you already submitted, holding the plan thread's live claim (pass its lease_id). cancel names children to cancel; add gives new children (the shape submit_plan takes, depends_on may name any child of the plan); rewire sets a child's depends_on afresh. Cancel and add the same key to replace a child: its dependents wait for the new one. A cancelled child's dependents stop waiting for it. Only children that are open and unclaimed can be cancelled or rewired: a claimed or finished one is refused, as is a fourth amendment of the same plan (error code -32010). reason is kept on each cancelled child. Everything happens in one transaction, or nothing does. Added children are held for review when the plan is held or one of them needs a threat model.
tools.name: amend_plan

tools.description: Declare what part of a repository this thread's work touches, so a swarm claiming from one queue never holds overlapping work. items lists {kind: path|glob|crate|lane|branch, value}; lane, crate and branch match exactly, path and glob by prefix (a glob counts up to its first wildcard). mode exclusive conflicts with any overlap, shared only with an exclusive one, and a branch is always exclusive. Footprints count only while the thread holds a live claim and free themselves when it ends. claim_next skips a thread whose footprint overlaps a live claim. On a claimed thread, a footprint that overlaps another live claim is refused with error code -32009 and data.conflicts (each with thread_id, assignee_id, lease_expires_at, kind, value), and nothing is stored: release the claim and requeue, or narrow the footprint. No items clears the footprint. repo is owner/name, or a GitHub clone URL.
tools.name: set_thread_footprint

tools.description: List the workspace's live claims with their footprints (thread_id, assignee_id, lease_expires_at, repo, mode, items, attributes), in one repository when repo is given. Only threads you may read are listed. Use it to defer work whose footprint would overlap before claiming.
tools.name: list_active_claims

tools.description: Add a task-dependency edge: the thread depends on depends_on_thread_id and stays blocked (won't be handed out by claim_next) until that dependency reaches a terminal state. Both threads must be in the same workspace.
tools.name: add_thread_dependency

tools.description: List the threads a task depends on and whether the task is ready to run. Returns {dependencies: a list of {thread_id, depends_on_thread_id, created_at}, ready}; ready is true when every dependency is closed or archived, and also when there are none. A thread that is not ready is not handed out by claim_next. Add and remove edges with add_thread_dependency and remove_thread_dependency, and use list_thread_dependents for the reverse direction. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_thread_dependencies

tools.description: Count one channel's open task threads as {open, ready, assigned, blocked, unclaimable}, to decide whether to add or remove workers. The counts partition open: ready is what claim_next_thread could hand out now, assigned is held by an assignee with a live lease, blocked is stalled on an explicit block, an unfinished dependency, a pending approval gate or a footprint conflict, and unclaimable is withheld until someone acts (parked, at its budget, or already holding a result). Use get_workspace_queue_depth for every channel of the workspace, and get_channel_occupancy for the same channel when you need held work split into claimed and working. Counts only threads you may read; on the DM channel, your own DMs. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_queue_depth

tools.description: Split one channel's open task threads into {open, queued, claimed, working, blocked} by what the holder is doing: claimed is held but not yet acknowledged with acknowledge_claim, and working is held and acknowledged, so a claimed count that stays high exposes an agent that took work and never started it. queued equals the ready count of get_queue_depth, and blocked is that tool's blocked plus unclaimable; the four buckets add up to open. Use get_queue_depth for the pool-sizing counts of the same channel, get_workspace_occupancy for the same split across the whole workspace, and get_run_occupancy for the threads of one producer run. Counts only threads you may read. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_channel_occupancy

tools.description: Count open task threads across every channel of your workspace that you may read, as {open, ready, assigned, blocked, unclaimable}: the sum of get_queue_depth over those channels, with the same field meanings. Use it to size a pool of workers that claim with claim_next_workspace_thread; use get_queue_depth for one channel, and get_workspace_occupancy for the claimed and working split. repo, engine and kind narrow the count exactly as they narrow claim_next_workspace_thread. With claimable_by set to me, only threads claim_next_workspace_thread would hand you count: reviews of your own model family's changes, threads you declined as your family's, threads needing a skill you lack, and everything while you are frozen are left out, so a seat can wake only when its own ready is above 0. A private channel's threads count only for its members and a DM's only for its participants. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_workspace_queue_depth

tools.description: Count your workspace's open task threads by stage, summed over every channel you can read, as {open, queued, claimed, working, blocked}. queued is claimable now, claimed is held on a live lease but not yet acknowledged, working is held and acknowledged, and blocked is parked or blocked; the last four add up to open. A private channel's threads count only for its members and a DM's only for its participants. Use get_channel_occupancy for one channel and get_workspace_queue_depth for the unclaimed-work view with filters. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_workspace_occupancy

tools.description: Track a pull request the change flow did not open (yours, from a session) on its task's thread, so the change sweep refreshes it and get_swarm_metrics counts it: its time to ready runs from the task's CLAIM: comment (else claimed_at, else now) to the ready-to-merge label, and its merge closes the task. The repository must be in the workspace egress allowlist (github or github_branch). A pull request another thread tracks is refused. The twin of PUT /threads/{id}/pull.
tools.name: register_thread_pull

tools.description: The workspace's swarm ramp metrics: per agent pull request the rounds it took, time to ready and to merge, whether it merged as delivered, its cost and whether it needs a look, with rollups per repository, engine, size, risk, provider and harness. Pull requests not yet seen closed are read from GitHub first when the server has a GitHub client. The twin of GET /workspaces/{id}/swarm-metrics.
tools.name: get_swarm_metrics

tools.description: The workspace's prepaid credits: balance_micros (USD micros, one USDC base unit each; below zero, overage went unpaid and the priced meters are cut off until a deposit covers it), whether this instance takes payment (enabled) and by which methods (usdc now; card next), the chain, receiving address and USDC contract, the overage price per meter, the open top-up intents and the recent ledger (deposits, charges, grants). Works past the allowance cutoff. The twin of GET /workspaces/{id}/credits.
tools.name: get_credits

tools.description: Ask to be paid: opens a top-up intent for usd dollars. method usdc (the default) answers the exact amount to send (amount_micros USDC base units, the dollars plus a small offset that names your workspace), the receiving address, the chain and its id, the USDC contract, an EIP-681 wallet link and expires_at (24 hours). With a wallet, pay that exact amount of USDC on that chain yourself; once the transfer has its confirmations the balance is credited and a cutoff on a priced meter lifts. A different amount is not matched. Without a wallet, ask with method card and hand the checkout_url it answers to a person; card is the next rail, and an instance that has not configured it says so. get_credits lists the methods this instance offers. Moves no money. Call it when a call is refused as past the free allowance (HTTP 402, or a tool error naming the meter). Works past the cutoff. At most 20 open intents per workspace. The twin of POST /workspaces/{id}/credits/top-ups.
tools.name: top_up_credits

tools.description: Block until the first event of any of the listed kinds arrives in your workspace (or in one thread) and return {log_id, event}, or null when timeout_ms lapses. Use it to wait on several event kinds at once or to replay the log; wait_for_ready, wait_for_claim_expired, wait_for_claim_failed, wait_for_landed and wait_for_blocked_resolved fix one kind, wait_for_result and wait_for_memory_block return a payload instead of the event, and wait_for_mention and wait_for_notification wait on one member's mentions or notifications. Pass the log_id of the last event you handled as after_log_id to replay the log first; a loop that must see every event passes it on every call, since an event between two calls is otherwise missed. An unknown kind name is refused, events in a private channel you are not in or a DM you are not part of never wake it, and timeout_ms 0 only replays and needs after_log_id. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: wait_for_event

tools.description: Find the thread an external reference points at: a Slack message (slack_channel and slack_ts: the thread whose result was posted as that message or into that Slack thread), a Slack channel alone (the thread it is linked to), or a GitHub pull request (repo and pr_number: the thread tracking it, linked to it, or delivering to it). Returns the thread, or null when nothing in your workspace that you may read matches. The twin of GET /workspaces/{id}/thread-lookup.
tools.name: find_thread

tools.description: Find a workspace's threads by their task attributes: equality filters over kind, engine, threat_model, size, linear_issue, repo, tier, lane and review_family, given as attr (attr.linear_issue=ENG-123 style pairs), plus engine, tier and lane as bare shorthand, and ref (ref.twin_of=<thread id> style: relation wire name to thread id) for threads holding that reference to that thread; a thread outside your workspace matches nothing (an unused relation is an empty result too). Combined with AND. A thread with no stored attributes matches the defaults it reads with (kind=change, threat_model=false); the other fields match only a stored value. Scoped to your own workspace (workspace_id omitted, the same; a foreign one is refused) and to threads you may read. Keyset-paginated like list_threads (limit, cursor, order; a cursor that is not a thread you can read in your workspace is refused); returned threads carry their attributes. The twin of GET /workspaces/{id}/threads.
tools.name: find_threads

tools.description: Home a producer's run_id on a thread as parent_run_id. Accepts the producer's string as-is (does not mint a parallel id). Empty / whitespace / over-long is rejected. Use when attributing nested work to a producer run; set_thread_result also auto-homes when the payload carries run_id.
tools.name: set_thread_lineage

tools.description: Read a thread's run lineage (parent_run_id + set_at), or null if none has been set.
tools.name: get_thread_lineage

tools.description: List threads in the caller's workspace that share a producer parent_run_id, oldest first. Nested children given the same value are included. Private-channel rows the caller cannot access are omitted. F7 mute is not consulted.
tools.name: list_run_threads

tools.description: Count the open threads that share one producer run id, as {parent_run_id, open, queued, claimed, working, blocked}: the split of get_channel_occupancy applied to every thread in your workspace whose lineage names that run, across channels. Use it to watch the nested work of one orchestrated run; attach the run id to a thread with set_thread_lineage and list those threads with list_run_threads. Counts only threads you may read and includes muted ones, and a run id that no thread uses returns zeros, not an error. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_run_occupancy

tools.description: Attach a task's structured result (arbitrary JSON). Upserts one result per thread and notifies waiters via a thread_result_set event. Use when finishing a task so a requester or parent can read the output. Fenced by your claim: pass claim_lease_id from the claim response; if the lease lapsed and someone else took the thread (or it was released), the call is refused (claim_lost) and nothing is stored, so stop the work. When the server sets MAIDAN_CHANGE_REFUSE_WORKFLOW_PATHS (its GitHub token cannot push workflow files), a maidan.change.result/1 with status changed, a github_branch target and a diff touching .github/workflows/ is refused with invalid params naming the files and nothing is stored: drop the workflow edit and set the result again.
tools.name: set_thread_result

tools.description: Read a task's structured result, or null if none has been produced yet.
tools.name: get_thread_result

tools.description: List thread results in the caller's workspace, newest first. Optional result_kind is an exact-match facet on the namespaced string (e.g. example.review.result/1), not a closed enum. Private-channel rows the caller cannot access are omitted.
tools.name: list_thread_results

tools.description: List per-target delivery status for a thread's structured result (disposition, external reference, last error). Empty means the result was not routed anywhere, which is valid. workspace:read + thread access.
tools.name: list_result_deliveries

tools.description: Re-enqueue one result delivery onto the egress outbox. Re-checks the workspace allowlist (an unblessed target stays skipped). Does not bump armed_revision. workspace:write + thread access.
tools.name: replay_result_delivery

tools.description: Set (or clear, by omitting owner_id) a thread's durable owner — the accountable party, distinct from the assignee/claimer. Once an owner is set, the claimer can no longer land (close/archive) its own work; the owner or another member must (separation of duties).
tools.name: set_thread_owner

tools.description: Rename a thread — give a titled thread a new name (e.g. name a post-derived child thread). The title must not be blank. A rename is metadata, not activity, so it does not float the thread in the recent-activity order.
tools.name: rename_thread

tools.description: Set a thread's persisted steer, the durable guidance a resuming or newly assigned agent should follow, replacing any earlier steer (the latest write wins), and return {thread_id, steer, steered_by, steered_at} with the caller as steered_by. The steer stays on the thread across claims and handoffs and emits no event; a reader picks it up with get_thread_steer. Use it for standing guidance rather than a one-off reply, which belongs in a message. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: set_thread_steer

tools.description: Read a thread's current steer, or null if none is set. A resuming or newly-assigned agent reads this to follow the current steering guidance.
tools.name: get_thread_steer

tools.description: Block until the task named by thread_id produces its result (thread_result_set) and return the result record {thread_id, result, produced_by, produced_at}, or null when the timeout lapses; this is the wait in spawn, wait, aggregate. Unlike the event waits it returns the stored result rather than an event, and it needs a thread_id. A live wait does not see a result that already exists: read it with get_thread_result first, or use get_dependency_results for every dependency result of a parent at once. since_log_id replays a result set on this thread after that log_id before waiting live. To put a deadline on a thread instead, use set_wait. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: wait_for_result

tools.description: Gather the structured results of a parent task's dependencies as a list of {thread_id, result} objects (result null if not produced yet), skipping dependencies you can't access. The spawn/wait/aggregate read for a parent task.
tools.name: get_dependency_results

tools.description: Declare a skill (free-form tag) for a member. Skill routing gates claim_next: a task is claimable by a member only if it holds all the task's required skills.
tools.name: add_member_skill

tools.description: List the skills a member has declared, ordered by skill, as records of member_id, skill and created_at. Declared skills decide which tasks the member is offered: claim_next_thread only hands over a thread whose required skills the member holds (see list_thread_required_skills), and governance skills confer authority over gates. A token can only read its own member's skills, so member_id must be the caller's own; another member's id is refused. Change the list with add_member_skill and remove_member_skill. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_member_skills

tools.description: Add a required skill to a task. Only a member holding every required skill can claim the task via claim_next_thread.
tools.name: add_thread_required_skill

tools.description: List the skills a task (thread) requires, ordered by skill, as records of thread_id, skill and created_at. claim_next_thread only hands the thread to a member who has declared every one of them, so call this to see why a member is not being offered a task. To change the list use add_thread_required_skill or remove_thread_required_skill; to see what a member has declared use list_member_skills. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.
tools.name: list_thread_required_skills

tools.description: Create a task schedule: when due, the sweeper creates a thread titled `title` in `channel_id` (or, when recipe_id is set, instantiates that recipe — parent + DAG children — instead). interval_secs omitted = one-shot; a positive value = recurring. first_run_at omitted = fire on the next tick.
tools.name: create_task_schedule

tools.description: List the caller's workspace task schedules (filtered to channels the caller can access).
tools.name: list_task_schedules

tools.description: Create a recipe: a reusable thread-type blueprint. spec = {params, definition_of_done, retry, children}, where each child is {key, title, required_skills, depends_on (sibling keys)}. Instantiating it (instantiate_recipe) builds a parent thread + a child per child + wires the DAG + attaches skills. NOT a recipe VM — a blueprint the room instantiates.
tools.name: create_recipe

tools.description: List the recipes in the caller's workspace, newest first, leaving out any recipe whose channel the caller cannot read. Each recipe carries id, workspace_id, channel_id, name, its spec (params, definition of done, retry policy and child sub-tasks), created_by and timestamps. Pass a recipe id to instantiate_recipe to build its threads, or to delete_recipe to remove it. Takes no arguments. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_recipes

tools.description: Instantiate a recipe into a parent thread + its DAG children (copy-on-fire: the recipe bytes are frozen into the run). params are validated against the recipe's declared params (required ones must be present). Returns the RecipeRun.
tools.name: instantiate_recipe

tools.description: List the caller's workspace secrets (metadata only — id, name, timestamps; NEVER the value). Use resolve_secret to fetch a value at exec.
tools.name: list_secrets

tools.description: Resolve a named secret to its value (the 'fetch at exec' path). The value is decrypted server-side and returned only in this response — it never enters the event log. Returns null-name error if the secret is unknown.
tools.name: resolve_secret

tools.description: List the hosts trusted with this workspace's secret values: on a webhook, automation HTTP or A2A push delivery to one of them, secret://<name> refs in the payload are replaced with the workspace's values; any other host gets the literal ref. Empty (the default) means no host gets a value. Requires secret:admin.
tools.name: list_secret_egress_hosts

tools.description: Trust a host with this workspace's secret values (idempotent). A listed host receives the value of every secret a payload bound for it names, so this needs secret:read as well as secret:admin. The host is a lowercase hostname or IPv4 address with no scheme, port, path or wildcard, and must be inside the instance ceiling when the operator set one. Audited.
tools.name: allow_secret_egress_host

tools.description: Stop trusting a host with this workspace's secret values; the next delivery to it carries the literal secret:// refs. Not found when the host was not listed. Requires secret:admin. Audited.
tools.name: revoke_secret_egress_host

tools.description: Freeze a member (the kill-switch): drops their active leases (releases their claimed threads) and makes claim_next refuse them. Returns the freeze record + the count released, and emits member_frozen to the workspace (the reason included). The member stays frozen until unfreeze_member. Requires token:admin. NOT a thread/workspace pause.
tools.name: freeze_member

tools.description: Lift a member's freeze so they can claim work again. Requires token:admin. Returns {unfrozen} (false if they were not frozen); an unfreeze that lifts a freeze emits member_unfrozen.
tools.name: unfreeze_member

tools.description: List the frozen members in the caller's workspace (member_id, frozen_at, frozen_by, reason). Requires token:admin.
tools.name: list_frozen_members

tools.description: Issue a read-only cross-organization ticket for one channel and an explicit artifact allowlist. Ownership is bound to the authenticated member. Lifetime is capped at 48 hours; the secret is returned once and only its hash is stored. Requires token:admin.
tools.name: create_share_ticket

tools.description: List share tickets and their explicit artifact scopes in the caller's workspace. Secrets are never returned after creation. Requires token:admin.
tools.name: list_share_tickets

tools.description: Immediately revoke a share ticket in the caller's workspace. Requires token:admin.
tools.name: revoke_share_ticket

tools.description: Export a workspace as a signed maidan.workspace.export/1 envelope. Tokens die on export: API tokens and secrets are omitted. A blank instance can verify the file without calling this host. Requires token:admin and MAIDAN_EXPORT_SIGNING_KEY.
tools.name: export_workspace

tools.description: Verify a signed workspace export without importing it. Fail-closed on tamper, a bad signature, stuffed secret fields, or a public key outside MAIDAN_EXPORT_VERIFY_KEYS when that pin is set. An empty pin checks integrity against the embedded key only. Requires token:admin.
tools.name: verify_workspace_export

tools.description: Verify then import a signed workspace export. mode new remaps ids into a fresh workspace; restore keeps original ids and fails if that workspace exists unless force is true. Tokens die on export: mint new tokens after import. Requires token:admin.
tools.name: import_workspace

tools.description: Hashed event-log snapshot for this workspace (getRepo-shaped, not MST/CAR). Header plus graph_hash is workspace:read. Pass include_graph true for the domain graph; that requires token:admin. Complements hash-chain verify of the retained suffix: this covers a pruned prefix so a peer can resume without trusting the host for history it never saw.
tools.name: get_log_snapshot

tools.description: Since-LSN catch-up page after a snapshot (or a prior page). Events have id greater than after_lsn, hash-chain checked from the predecessor. A pruned-gap cursor fails closed and names the snapshot path to refetch; a broken chain fails closed. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: catch_up_events

tools.description: Verify the retained event-log hash chain for a workspace. Returns the chain report when intact; fails closed on a splice or rewrite. Twin of GET /workspaces/{id}/events/verify. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: verify_event_chain

tools.description: Tombstone and deletion explorer for this workspace. Soft-deleted messages (body already cleared) plus, when include_purged is true, hard-purged reconstructions from MessageTombstoned events. Private-channel and DM rows the caller cannot access are omitted. Twin of GET /workspaces/{id}/tombstones. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_tombstones

tools.description: Incoming pointers at a message: RelationKind reverse edges plus pins, reactions, and votes. Mentions are outgoing and omitted. Works on a retained tombstone; fails not-found after hard purge. Twin of GET /messages/{id}/backlinks. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_message_backlinks

tools.description: Count the events in the workspace's event log by event kind, as {workspace_id, total, counts} where counts lists {kind, count} ordered by count descending then kind, and kinds with no events are left out. It answers what has happened (messages posted, claims expired, threads landed), not how much work is queued: use get_queue_depth or get_channel_occupancy for queue state. Optionally narrowed to one channel or one thread; there is no time window, and events on threads you may not read, including private channels you are not in, are excluded from the totals. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_kind_census

tools.description: Create a labeled memory block — a Letta-shaped shared object {label, description, limit, read_only, value} in the workspace that a thread can attach to (a room object). It is how a parent watches a child's result block without a nested runtime: not a transcript, not RAG. Concurrent-safe on the label (re-creating a label returns the existing block). The caller owns it.
tools.name: create_memory_block

tools.description: Get a memory block by label within the caller's workspace, or null if none. This is the watch-a-child's-result-block read (poll it).
tools.name: get_memory_block

tools.description: List every memory block in the caller's workspace, ordered by label, as a list of objects with id, workspace_id, label, description (omitted when unset), char_limit (omitted when unset), read_only, value, owner_id, revision, created_at and updated_at. All blocks come back at once with their full values, with no paging or limit, so the result can be large. To read one block by label use get_memory_block; to see only the blocks attached to a thread use list_thread_memory_blocks. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_memory_blocks

tools.description: Full-rewrite a memory block's value by label, at the revision you read. Read the block with get_memory_block, change its value, and pass its revision as expected_revision. If another write landed since, the call is refused: read it again, redo the change and retry. A read-only block or a value over the block's char limit is rejected. Use this to publish a result other threads watch.
tools.name: set_memory_block_value

tools.description: Attach a memory block, named by label, to a thread so the thread carries it as a shared object: how a parent hands a block to a child. Returns {attached: true} when newly attached and {attached: false} when it was already attached. The block must already exist in your workspace (create_memory_block makes one; an unknown label is refused), and attaching never changes its value. list_thread_memory_blocks shows what a thread carries and detach_memory_block removes the link. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: attach_memory_block

tools.description: Remove a memory block's attachment from one thread, identified by block id. The block and its value stay in the workspace and other threads keep it; delete_memory_block deletes the block itself and attach_memory_block is the opposite call. Returns {detached: true}, or {detached: false} when the block was not attached, so repeating the call is safe. Get block ids from list_thread_memory_blocks. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: detach_memory_block

tools.description: List the memory blocks attached to a thread (its room objects), ordered by label. Each block carries id, workspace_id, label, description, char_limit, read_only, value, owner_id, revision and timestamps. This shows only what is attached to the one thread; list_memory_blocks lists every block in the workspace, and get_memory_block reads one by label. Attach and detach with attach_memory_block and detach_memory_block. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.
tools.name: list_thread_memory_blocks

tools.description: Block until the memory block with the given label is rewritten and return the block with its fresh value, or null when the timeout lapses. This is how a parent watches a child's result block; it sees only rewrites after it subscribes and has no log replay, so read the current value with get_memory_block first. Use wait_for_result to await a task's result instead of a block, and wait_for_event for several event kinds. Scoped to your workspace. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: wait_for_memory_block

tools.description: Set (upsert) a thread's required-reviewers gate (G5): required_count distinct qualifying approvals before it can close. An approval qualifies when the reviewer is neither the owner nor the assignee (separation of duties) and, when a named reviewer set exists, is in it. A refutes edge also blocks close. max_rounds is how many send-backs one cycle allows before a person decides whether it goes around again (default 3; 0 leaves it uncapped). Omit max_rounds to leave the cap as it is. Tightening the cap needs thread:transition. Raising or removing it needs channel:admin. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: set_review_requirement

tools.description: Name a member as an eligible reviewer for a thread. While no reviewer is named, any qualifying member may review; once one is named, only the named members count, so adding the first reviewer narrows who can approve. Returns {added: true} for a new reviewer and {added: false} when the member was already named, so repeating the call is safe. The member must be in your workspace. Use list_reviewers to see the set, remove_reviewer to take one off, and set_review_requirement for how many approvals the thread needs. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: add_reviewer

tools.description: Submit a review decision as the caller (G5): approve or request_changes. The reviewer is you; an owner/assignee may submit but it will not count toward the requirement (separation of duties). request_changes on an in_review thread, from its owner or a reviewer whose approval would count, sends it back to open for rework: it is claimable again, earlier approvals are dismissed, and your note appears in its context as change_requests. request_changes needs a note saying what to change; approve may carry one. approve also needs evidence_root, the root from get_review_packet of what you were shown: it is refused when the thread was handed over again or changed since, and only an approval bound to the latest packet counts toward the close. Every verdict appends a review_submitted event (the note stays in the review history), and a request_changes notifies the thread's last worker. Re-submitting changes your decision. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: submit_review

tools.description: Read a thread's review standing: required_count, approvals (distinct qualifying), and approvals_met. This is the approval side of the close-gate; a refutes edge is checked separately when closing.
tools.name: get_review_status

tools.description: List each reviewer's current decision on a thread, ordered by creation time. A row has reviewer_id, decision (approve or request_changes), note, the delegate actor_id if one submitted it, evidence_root, head_sha and dismissed_at, which is set on an approval that a later change request invalidated. Re-submitting replaces a reviewer's row, so earlier verdicts are in list_review_history; whether the requirement is met is in get_review_status. Submit with submit_review. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.
tools.name: list_reviews

tools.description: List every verdict submitted on a thread, oldest first (reviewer, decision, note, delegate, recorded_at). list_reviews shows each reviewer's current decision; a re-submission replaces it there but its earlier verdicts stay here.
tools.name: list_review_history

tools.description: Record a land-gate pointer on a thread: status pass or fail, optional artifact_sha, optional land green/amber/red. The room holds the pointer; an external verifier records pass/fail. A qualifying green pass (land-gate-skilled member who is not the implementer) is required to close once the gate is armed. Amber is flags-then-still-engages and is not a land. Requires thread:transition. The caller must have declared the land_gate skill.
tools.name: set_land_gate

tools.description: Read a thread's land-gate standing: required, pointer, land (green/amber/red), landable. No pointer is vacuous green. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_land_gate

tools.description: List every land-gate verdict recorded on a thread, oldest first (status, land, artifact_sha, recorder, delegate, recorded_at). get_land_gate shows the latest pointer; a later pointer or clearing the gate leaves earlier verdicts here. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_land_gate_history

tools.description: Arm the land-gate close-gate on a thread that has no land-gate pointer yet, so a transition to closed is refused until a qualifying green pass is recorded with set_land_gate. An existing pointer is left unchanged, and repeating the call changes nothing. Returns the standing {required, pointer, land, landable}; read it later with get_land_gate and remove the gate with clear_land_gate. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: require_land_gate

tools.description: Clear a thread's land-gate pointer and requirement. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: clear_land_gate

tools.description: Define (or redefine) a term in the workspace's shared glossary — the canonical term -> definition so agents use words the same way (the anti-drift pin; the target of a `defines` reference). Upserts on the term.
tools.name: set_glossary_term

tools.description: Look up one term's canonical definition in the workspace glossary. Returns null when the term is undefined.
tools.name: get_glossary_term

tools.description: List all defined terms in the workspace's shared glossary, ordered by term.
tools.name: list_glossary_terms

tools.description: Block until a task becomes ready, meaning its last blocking dependency reached a terminal state (thread_ready), and return the ThreadReady event, or null when the timeout lapses. It answers only that dependency signal: use wait_for_blocked_resolved for an explicit block being cleared, wait_for_claim_expired for a lapsed claim, wait_for_event for several kinds at once, and claim_next_thread to take ready work that already exists. Scoped to channel_id when given, else any thread you may read in the workspace. since_log_id replays a ThreadReady recorded after that log_id before waiting live; without it only readiness signalled after the call counts. To put a deadline on a thread instead, use set_wait. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: wait_for_ready

tools.description: Block until a claim's lease lapses and its thread is reclaimed (claim_expired), the signal that an agent holding work died or stopped renewing, and return the ClaimExpired event (member_id is the dead holder), or null when the timeout lapses. Use wait_for_claim_failed for a run stopped for going over its budget, and wait_for_event to wait on several kinds. The reclaim happens in the claim reaper within seconds, or in the next claim_next_thread. A thread in review is reaped like an open one: its implementer must keep renewing through review, or the claim is reaped and a changes-requested thread reopens unheld. Scoped to channel_id when given, else any thread you may read in the workspace; since_log_id replays an expiry recorded in the gap before this call subscribes. To put a deadline on a thread instead, use set_wait. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: wait_for_claim_expired

tools.description: Block until a claimed run is stopped for going over its budget (claim_failed) and return the ClaimFailed event (member_id is the stopped holder, reason the budget axis: tokens, usd, turns or wall), or null when the timeout lapses. A report_usage past a limit releases the claim, dead-letters the run and emits it; a reclaim whose worked time put the thread over budget emits it too. Use wait_for_claim_expired for a holder that died or stopped renewing instead, and wait_for_event to wait on several kinds. Scoped to channel_id when given, else any thread you may read in the workspace; since_log_id replays a stop recorded in the gap before this call subscribes. To put a deadline on a thread instead, use set_wait. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: wait_for_claim_failed

tools.description: Block until an explicit dispatch block on a thread is cleared (clear_thread_block emits blocked_resolved) and return the BlockedResolved event (the reason that cleared, resolved_by), or null when the timeout lapses. It answers only a cleared block, not a dependency finishing (wait_for_ready) or a lapsed claim (wait_for_claim_expired); get_thread_block reads the current block. Scoped to thread_id and/or channel_id when given, else any thread you may read in the workspace; clearing a thread that was not blocked emits nothing. since_log_id replays a clear recorded in the gap before this call subscribes. To put a deadline on a thread instead, use set_wait. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: wait_for_blocked_resolved

tools.description: Block until a thread's linked GitHub pull request is merged (thread_landed) and return the ThreadLanded event (repo, pr_number, merged_by, merge_commit_sha, title), or null when the timeout lapses. The workspace records the landing but does not change the thread's state; use wait_for_event to wait on several kinds, and wait_for_result for a task's result rather than a merge. Scoped to thread_id and/or channel_id when given, else any landing in the workspace that you may read; since_log_id replays a landing recorded in the gap before this call subscribes. To put a deadline on a thread instead, use set_wait. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: wait_for_landed

tools.description: List the recent @mentions of a member, newest first, as {message_id, member_id, created_at} rows. A row names the message but does not carry its text; read the message with list_messages on its thread. Mentions made in a private channel or DM the member cannot read are left out. Use get_inbox for mentions plus the read cursor and wait_for_mention to block until the next one. member_id must be your own. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_mentions

tools.description: A member's mention inbox: recent mentions plus the read-cursor, so an agent can find what it hasn't seen. Mentions only; for everything waiting on the member (assigned tasks, requested reviews, open approval gates and unread mentions), use get_waiting_inbox.
tools.name: get_inbox

tools.description: Move a member's mention inbox read-cursor forward to a given instant, so mentions at or before it count as read, and return the updated inbox: items (up to 50), unread_count and last_read_at. The cursor never moves backward, so an earlier instant than the current cursor changes nothing. This is the cursor for get_inbox; notifications are cleared with mark_notification_read or mark_all_notifications_read instead. The member_id must be the caller. Requires member:self.
tools.name: mark_inbox_read

tools.description: Block until the member is next @mentioned (mention_recorded) and return the mention event, or null when the timeout lapses. member_id must be your own. Use wait_for_notification to wake for any unread notification, such as an event routed to you as owner or follower, not only mentions; get_inbox and list_mentions read mentions that already exist, so drain those first. since_log_id (your high-water log_id from the last drain) replays a mention recorded in the gap before this call subscribes; omit it for pure-live behaviour. Mentions in a private channel or DM you cannot read are skipped. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: wait_for_mention

tools.description: List a member's per-recipient notifications, newest first. Set unread_only to see just the unread ones. Each carries its kind, thread_id, the thread's title and a short reason read from the event that caused it, enough for a digest line. The durable inbox the notification router fills; drain it here, then wait_for_notification for new ones.
tools.name: list_notifications

tools.description: The waiting-on-you inbox, everything needing a member's attention: their assigned non-terminal threads, the reviews requested from them (review_request: a thread in review naming them as a reviewer, without their approval yet), the reviews that name no reviewer and fall to them (unassigned_review: a thread in review with no named reviewer that they own, or that nobody owns when they are a workspace admin), the workspace's pending approval gates, and their unread mentions. Oldest-waiting first, each aged against sla_secs (default 86400 = 24h) with an overdue flag. One member's queue, not @everyone. For mentions alone, with a read-cursor you advance with mark_inbox_read, use get_inbox.
tools.name: get_waiting_inbox

tools.description: A member's notifications collapsed into per-thread groups, newest-activity first — a busy thread shows as one group (with its count, unread_count, and latest notification) instead of flooding the flat list. limit bounds how many notifications are scanned.
tools.name: list_notifications_grouped

tools.description: A member's buried decisions — task results (decisions) produced by someone else in a channel or thread the member follows, since a given instant (default 7 days ago), newest first. The decisions the digest surfaces, queryable directly.
tools.name: list_buried_decisions

tools.description: Return a member's unread work-lifecycle notifications since an instant, rolled up per channel: {member_id, since, channels: a list of {channel_id, results, gates, stuck}, spend_usd_micros, cost_per_completed_task_usd_micros}. results counts task results set, gates counts approval requests, and stuck counts claims expired, unacknowledged, stalled or failed plus wait timeouts; a null channel_id is the bucket for notifications with no channel. The spend figures are lifetime workspace totals, not limited to since. It is a notification view, not analytics: use usage_rollup for spend and list_notifications for the items. member_id must be your own. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_manager_digest

tools.description: Return {count}, the number of unread notifications a member has, for a badge. Notifications that are read, snoozed until a later time, or from a private channel or DM the member can no longer read are not counted. List the notifications with list_notifications and clear them with mark_all_notifications_read. member_id must be your own. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_unread_count

tools.description: Mark one of a member's notifications read (recipient-scoped; marked=false if the id isn't this member's). Requires member:self.
tools.name: mark_notification_read

tools.description: Snooze one of a member's notifications until an RFC 3339 instant — it drops out of the inbox and unread badge until then, and resurfaces once the snooze lapses. Recipient-scoped (snoozed=false if the id isn't this member's). Requires member:self.
tools.name: snooze_notification
