tools.description: Block until you have an unread notification of any kind (a mention, or an event routed to you as owner or follower) and return it with the thread's title and a short reason, or null when the timeout lapses. Use wait_for_mention to wake on mentions only, and list_notifications to read what already waits. It reads the notification ledger, so with since_log_id (the highest source_log_id you have seen) it returns the oldest unread notification after it, including one written while you were not waiting; omitted, only notifications for events after the call count. It never marks the notification read; use mark_notification_read for that. member_id must be your own. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: wait_for_notification

tools.description: Set a member's mute preference for an event kind (kind is snake_case, e.g. mention_recorded). When muted, the router stops writing notifications of that kind for this member. Requires member:self.
tools.name: set_notification_pref

tools.description: List a member's notification preferences as {member_id, kind, muted, updated_at} rows, one per event kind the member has set. A kind with no row is not muted and still notifies. Change a preference with set_notification_pref; list_notifications returns the notifications themselves and get_unread_count their count. member_id must be your own. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_notification_prefs

tools.description: Set a member's email delivery mode: immediate (a per-notification email) or digest (a periodic rollup instead). The two are mutually exclusive. Requires member:self.
tools.name: set_delivery_mode

tools.description: Return {mode}, how a member's email notifications are delivered: immediate (one email per notification) or digest (a periodic rollup instead). A member who never set a mode reads immediate. Change it with set_delivery_mode. It returns neither the email address (get_member_email) nor mute settings (list_notification_prefs). member_id must be your own. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_delivery_mode

tools.description: Set the address a member's email notifications are delivered to, replacing any address already stored, and return {member_id, email, updated_at}. The value is trimmed and refused unless it contains an at sign and is at least 3 characters; deeper validation happens when mail is sent. Read the current address with get_member_email and clear it with delete_member_email. The member_id must be the caller. Requires member:self.
tools.name: set_member_email

tools.description: Get a member's delivery email address (null when unset).
tools.name: get_member_email

tools.description: Clear a member's delivery email address (opt out of email). Returns {deleted}. Requires member:self.
tools.name: delete_member_email

tools.description: Follow a channel so the member is notified of new messages there even without a mention (honors mutes). Requires access to the channel. Requires member:self.
tools.name: follow_channel

tools.description: Stop following a channel (removed=false if not following). Requires member:self.
tools.name: unfollow_channel

tools.description: List the channels a member follows as {member_id, channel_id, created_at} rows; activity in a followed channel notifies the member. Change the list with follow_channel and unfollow_channel, and use list_thread_follows or list_member_follows for threads and members. member_id must be your own. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_channel_follows

tools.description: Follow a thread so the member is notified of new messages in it even without a mention (honors mutes). Requires access to the thread. Requires member:self.
tools.name: follow_thread

tools.description: Stop following a thread (removed=false if not following). Requires member:self.
tools.name: unfollow_thread

tools.description: List the threads a member follows, newest follow first, as records of member_id, thread_id and created_at. Following makes the member a recipient of notifications for that thread; change it with follow_thread and unfollow_thread. For channel follows use list_channel_follows, and for member-occupancy subscriptions use list_member_follows. A token can only read its own member's follows, so member_id must be the caller's own. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_thread_follows

tools.description: Follow another same-workspace member's work occupancy. Self-follow is rejected. Requires member:self.
tools.name: follow_member

tools.description: Get a member's live occupancy: ephemeral presence plus assigned non-terminal threads visible to the caller.
tools.name: get_member_occupancy

tools.description: Stop following another member's work occupancy (removed=false if not following). Requires member:self.
tools.name: unfollow_member

tools.description: List the member-occupancy subscriptions a member owns, newest first, as records of follower_id, followed_id and created_at. A follower receives the followed member's work-lifecycle notifications and can read that member's presence and assigned work. Change them with follow_member and unfollow_member; for thread follows use list_thread_follows and for channel follows list_channel_follows. A token can only read its own member's subscriptions, so member_id must be the caller's own. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_member_follows

tools.description: List the messages in a thread, oldest first, excluding withdrawn (tombstoned) ones. Each message has id, author_id, body, metadata, content, posted_at, edited_at and origin. It returns the first limit messages with no cursor, so a long thread's later messages are not reachable here; use get_thread_context for a prompt-ready pack with message cursors and a token budget, or search_messages to find messages by text. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.
tools.name: list_messages

tools.description: Post a message to a thread as the authenticated member and return the stored message (id, thread_id, author_id, body, metadata, content, posted_at). Send body for plain text or content for typed blocks; when body is empty it is derived from the blocks, and sending neither is refused. A closed thread still takes messages, while a deleted or archived thread refuses them. The post appends a MessagePosted event, records each @handle mention and publishes a mention event for it, and runs the registered slash command when the body begins with /name (see register_slash_command). For a DM conversation id use post_dm_message. Requires message:post.
tools.name: post_message

tools.description: Seed a new titled work thread from a source message (the write side of 're-ask'), linked by a seeded_from reference edge. inclusion: 'pointer' (default, edge only) or 'quote' (a first message quoting the source). The source is untouched; N seeds per source. Lineage is queryable via list_references (dst=the source, relation=seeded_from).
tools.name: seed_from_message

tools.description: Rewrite your own message in place, keeping its id and author, with a new body, new typed content or new metadata. Only the author can edit: another member's message can be tombstoned with tombstone_message, not rewritten, and a tombstoned message cannot be edited. Omitted content and metadata keep their current values, and sending neither body nor content is refused. The edit emits a message_edited event, which reindexes the message for search; earlier versions stay readable with list_message_edits. Returns the updated message. Requires message:post.
tools.name: edit_message

tools.description: Record that a member is mentioned in a message, for a mention that is not written as an @handle in the text. The mention appears in the member's list_mentions and notifications and wakes any wait_for_mention on them; a mention_recorded event is emitted on every call, though a repeat keeps one mention row. Posting a message that contains @handle text already records those mentions, so use this only for explicit extra mentions. The member must belong to the message's workspace, otherwise the call is not found. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: record_mention

tools.description: Cast a vote on a message. kind is approve, request_changes, or ack. Any other kind is rejected. An emoji is a reaction, not a vote kind. You hold at most one verdict per message: approve replaces your request_changes and the other way round, and ack stands beside either. Optional confidence (0..1) for weighted consensus; re-casting the same kind updates your confidence. retract_vote takes a vote back.
tools.name: cast_vote

tools.description: Take back your own vote of one kind on a message. Removing a vote you do not hold changes nothing. Returns whether a vote was removed.
tools.name: retract_vote

tools.description: Add the caller's emoji reaction to a message. A member holds at most one reaction per emoji per message, so repeating it keeps a single reaction, and a reaction_added event is emitted on each call. Returns {ok: true}. Remove it with remove_reaction and read reactions with list_reactions. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: add_reaction

tools.description: Remove the caller's own emoji reaction from a message; other members' reactions are untouched. Returns {removed: true} when a reaction was deleted and {removed: false} when the caller had not reacted with that emoji, and emits a reaction_removed event only in the first case. Reverse it with add_reaction. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: remove_reaction

tools.description: List the emoji reactions on a message, oldest first. Each row is one member's one emoji, with message_id, member_id, emoji and created_at; reactions are not aggregated into counts. Add and remove them with add_reaction and remove_reaction. Requires workspace:read and read access to the message's thread.
tools.name: list_reactions

tools.description: Pin a message in a thread so it is listed by list_pins, recording the caller as the pinner. The message must belong to that thread, otherwise the call is refused. Pinning an already pinned message keeps a single pin. It emits a message_pinned event and returns {ok: true}. Reverse it with unpin_message. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: pin_message

tools.description: Remove a message's pin in a thread. Returns {removed: true} and appends a MessageUnpinned event only when the message was pinned; otherwise {removed: false} and no event. The message itself stays in the thread, and a pin set by another member can be removed too. See the pins with list_pins and pin with pin_message. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: unpin_message

tools.description: List the pinned messages of a thread, oldest pin first, as records of thread_id, message_id, the pinning member_id and created_at. It returns references only, not message text; read the bodies with list_messages or get_thread_context. Pin and unpin with pin_message and unpin_message. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.
tools.name: list_pins

tools.description: Create a typed edge from a source thread or message to a destination thread or message in the same workspace, and return the reference (id, src_kind, src_id, dst_kind, dst_id, relation, created_at). Refused when both ends are the same entity, an end does not exist, the ends are in different workspaces, the identical edge exists already, or a depends, supersedes or duplicates edge would close a cycle. Appends a ReferenceAdded event; read edges back with list_references. For task ordering that holds back claim_next use add_thread_dependency instead. Requires workspace:write and read access to both ends.
tools.name: add_reference

tools.description: List references FROM a source (forward) or TO a target (reverse — 'what references this'), optionally filtered by relation. Provide exactly one of the src_kind+src_id or dst_kind+dst_id pair.
tools.name: list_references

tools.description: Store a file in the workspace's content-addressed artifact store from base64 bytes and register its metadata, returning the artifact record with its sha256, size_bytes, kind and mime_type. Identical bytes share one sha256, and uploading them again overwrites the workspace's recorded kind and mime_type and emits another artifact_upserted event. The whole request must fit the server's request body limit (2 MiB by default); for larger files use begin_artifact_multipart, which needs an S3 backend. The upload is refused, and nothing stored, when the workspace is over its stored-bytes allowance or when a screenshot, recording or attachment would exceed its media quota. Use link_thread_artifact to attach the result to a thread as evidence. Requires artifact:upload.
tools.name: upload_artifact

tools.description: Start an S3 multipart upload for a large artifact (requires S3 backend).
tools.name: begin_artifact_multipart

tools.description: Upload one part of a multipart artifact upload begun with begin_artifact_multipart, and return {part_number, etag}. Keep the etag of every part and pass them all to complete_artifact_multipart; discard the upload with abort_artifact_multipart. Refused for an empty part, invalid base64, a part_number outside 1 to 10000, an upload that belongs to another workspace, or a workspace that is over its stored-bytes allowance. Needs the S3 artifact backend and artifact:upload; for content that fits in one call use upload_artifact.
tools.name: upload_artifact_multipart_part

tools.description: Finish a multipart upload: join the parts, content-address the result by SHA-256 and register it as an artifact in your workspace. Returns the artifact (id, sha256, size_bytes, mime_type, kind, uploaded_by, created_at) and appends an ArtifactUpserted event; read it back with get_artifact_metadata or get_artifact. Refused, with nothing stored, when the workspace is over its stored-bytes allowance or the result would exceed its media quota. Needs the S3 artifact backend and artifact:upload; the parts come from upload_artifact_multipart_part.
tools.name: complete_artifact_multipart

tools.description: Abort a multipart upload begun with begin_artifact_multipart and delete its temporary parts, so nothing is registered as an artifact. Returns {aborted: true}; storage cleanup is best effort, so a storage error is not reported. Use it when a part upload failed or the object is no longer wanted, and use complete_artifact_multipart to finish the upload instead. Needs the S3 artifact backend and artifact:upload, and the upload must belong to your workspace.
tools.name: abort_artifact_multipart

tools.description: Return one artifact's metadata by its SHA-256 digest: id, sha256, size_bytes, mime_type, filename, kind, uploaded_by and created_at, without the bytes (get_artifact returns metadata plus content_base64). An artifact from another workspace, or one tied only to a private channel or DM you cannot read, is NotFound, the same as a missing one. A malformed digest is refused as invalid. Find digests with list_thread_artifacts or in an upload result. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_artifact_metadata

tools.description: Search the messages in a workspace by lexical, semantic or hybrid match, best hit first, optionally narrowed by channel, author, author kind and a time window. Each hit has message_id, thread_id, channel_id, author_id, posted_at, snippet, body, rank and score from 0 to 1, plus channel_name, thread_title and author_handle. Private channels and DMs the caller cannot read are never searched. Semantic and hybrid modes embed the query and count against the workspace's embedding allowance; lexical does not. To list a thread's messages in order use list_messages instead. Requires search:query.
tools.name: search_messages

tools.description: Register a workspace slash command: a message posted as /name text then runs the handler. With handler_kind http, Maidan POSTs a JSON payload (command, name, text, workspace_id, channel_id, thread_id, author_id, message_id) signed in the X-Maidan-Signature header to handler_target, and this call returns {command, secret} with the signing secret. With mcp_tool it runs the named MCP tool and returns the command. The name must not be in use by an active command; list them with list_slash_commands and free a name with revoke_slash_command. Requires workspace:write; mcp_tool also needs the capability the target tool requires, plus channel:admin when that tool is not read-only.
tools.name: register_slash_command

tools.description: List the workspace's registered slash commands that have not been revoked, ordered by name. Each has id, name, description, handler_kind (http, mcp_tool or wasi), handler_target and enabled; signing secrets are never returned. Add one with register_slash_command and remove one with revoke_slash_command. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_slash_commands

tools.description: Register a hook that fires when a thread in the workspace changes state, for every matching transition, and return it. An http hook POSTs the transition as signed JSON to the target URL with X-Maidan-Event and X-Maidan-Signature headers; its response also carries the signing secret, which list_fsm_hooks never returns. An mcp_tool hook calls the named tool with workspace_id, channel_id, thread_id, actor_id, from_state and to_state. The hook runs with the registering token's authority and is skipped, with an audit row, once that token is revoked or no longer holds workspace:admin. Each call creates a new hook; remove one with revoke_fsm_hook. Requires workspace:admin.
tools.name: register_fsm_hook

tools.description: List the workspace's registered FSM automation hooks that have not been revoked, oldest first. Each has id, label, from_state and to_state (null means any state), handler_kind, handler_target and enabled; the http signing secret is returned only when the hook is registered. Add a hook with register_fsm_hook and remove one with revoke_fsm_hook. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_fsm_hooks

tools.description: Pack thread messages, edits, references, FSM history, and the workspace glossary for agent prompts. Edits are lean by default (id/editor/timestamp only); pass include_edits=true for full before/after bodies. The glossary (canonical term definitions) is included by default when non-empty; pass include_glossary=false to drop it. Pass as_of=<event_id> to replay the thread as it stood at that event-log id (deterministic over the immutable log; audit / re-ask from before a tangent). Pass token_budget=<n> to cap the message page by estimated tokens: the opening message and the recent tail are kept, the middle is folded into an auditable elision marker in fixed blocks. The result is two text parts: the stable prefix (workspace boot, brief, messages) and the volatile tail (state, lease, cursors, prefix sha256). Those strings are the bytes REST returns with split=true.
tools.name: get_thread_context

tools.description: Freeze the assembled context pack (live or as_of) into the content-addressed artifact store — a tamper-evident, deduped record of exactly what the agent was handed. Same params as get_thread_context; returns the artifact (kind=context_snapshot). Requires artifact:upload. Fetch the bytes via the artifact sha.
tools.name: snapshot_thread_context

tools.description: Pack a workspace for one prompt: the workspace record, the channels you can see (public ones, and private ones you belong to) sorted by name, a page of live threads (oldest first, only ones you can read) each with its messages, references and FSM transitions, and the glossary once at the top level. thread_limit sets the page size (default 10, max 50), and next_thread_cursor, when present, is passed back as thread_cursor for the next page. Use get_thread_context for a single thread with edits and replay options, and list_threads or find_threads to locate threads without packing them. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_workspace_context

tools.description: Human-in-the-loop gate: open a durable approval gate and return {status: input_required, gate_id} without blocking. A human resolves it later (accept/decline/cancel) over the /ui; poll get_approval_gate for the outcome. Silence is never consent. Pass thread_id to make it a claim gate — while the gate is pending, claim_next will not hand that thread to an agent.
tools.name: request_approval

tools.description: Poll a durable approval gate by id. Returns the gate — state is pending until a human answers, then accepted/declined/cancelled with any content they supplied — or null if no such gate exists in your workspace. Hosts with MCP Apps show it as an inline approval card.
tools.name: get_approval_gate

tools.description: Decide a pending approval gate: accept or decline, with an optional note. Decline takes effect at once. Accept takes effect at once only for a token holding approval:grant, on a gate below the workspace's confirmation threshold (by default every gate is at or above it). Otherwise you get {status: confirmation_required, confirmation_url}: a one-time link the person opens in the Maidan console and confirms, signed in as themselves. Clients that declare URL-mode elicitation are shown the same link through elicitation. You cannot confirm for the person; do not retry, poll get_approval_gate. Nobody accepts a gate they requested. The decision records which client you used and that a model asked.
tools.name: approval_decide

tools.description: Link a Slack channel to a Maidan thread so the projector bridges messages both ways. The workspace/channel and attribution member come from the authenticated caller and thread. Requires workspace:write + access to the thread.
tools.name: link_slack_channel

tools.description: List the Slack channel links in your workspace. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_slack_channel_links

tools.description: Remove a Slack channel link in your workspace. Returns {unlinked: bool} (false if no such link belongs to your workspace). Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: unlink_slack_channel

tools.description: Link a GitHub issue/PR to a Maidan thread so the projector bridges messages both ways. The workspace/channel and attribution member come from the authenticated caller and thread. Requires workspace:write + access to the thread.
tools.name: link_github_issue

tools.description: List the GitHub issue/PR links in your workspace. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_github_issue_links

tools.description: Remove a GitHub issue/PR link in your workspace. Returns {unlinked: bool} (false if no such link belongs to your workspace). Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: unlink_github_issue

tools.description: Withdraw a message. Same store path as DELETE /messages/{id}: message:post, plus channel:admin when the caller is not the author.
tools.name: tombstone_message

tools.description: Open a group DM among at least three workspace members. Same store path as POST /workspaces/{wid}/group-dms. The opener is added if the member list leaves them out. Requires message:post. This writes a conversation.
tools.name: open_group_dm

tools.description: List group DMs for one member. member_id must be the caller. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_group_dms

tools.description: Fetch one group DM conversation by id as {id, workspace_id, thread_id, title, member_ids, created_at, updated_at}. Only a participant can read it: any other member is refused, and the conversation must be in your workspace. Use list_group_dms to find the group DMs a member is in, open_group_dm to start one, and post_group_dm_message to write to it. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_group_dm

tools.description: Post a text message as the caller into a group DM they take part in, and return the stored message. @handle mentions in the body are recorded and notified, and a message from a human clears the thread's declared agent status. It is for group DMs only: use post_dm_message for a 1:1 DM, post_message for a channel thread, and open_group_dm or list_group_dms to get the conversation id. A caller who is not a participant is refused. Requires message:post.
tools.name: post_group_dm_message

tools.description: Remove one dependency edge: thread_id no longer depends on depends_on_thread_id. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: remove_thread_dependency

tools.description: List the dependency edges that point at a thread, which are the tasks it blocks, oldest first. Each edge is thread_id (the waiting task), depends_on_thread_id (the thread you passed) and created_at. For the other direction, what this thread itself waits on and whether it is ready to run, use list_thread_dependencies. Edges are created with add_thread_dependency. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_thread_dependents

tools.description: Clear the run-lineage row for a thread. NotFound when no row exists. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: clear_thread_lineage

tools.description: Remove a declared skill from a member. A routing tag can be removed only from yourself. The governance skills land_gate, pre-review and review, which gates read as qualification, can also be removed from any member of your workspace by a caller holding channel:admin. Returns {ok: true}, or NotFound when the member does not hold that skill. Removing a skill changes which tasks claim_next hands the member and who can satisfy a gate; declare skills with add_member_skill and read them with list_member_skills. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: remove_member_skill

tools.description: Remove one required skill from a thread, so the thread no longer asks for it when work is routed to members by declared skill. It returns {ok: true}, or not found when that skill was not required on the thread. Use list_thread_required_skills to see the current set and add_thread_required_skill to add one. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: remove_thread_required_skill

tools.description: Delete a memory block by id. A block in another workspace is NotFound. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: delete_memory_block

tools.description: Permanently remove a term, with its definition and aliases, from the workspace glossary. The glossary rides in get_workspace_context, so the term drops out of later context packs. Use set_glossary_term to redefine a term instead of deleting it, and list_glossary_terms to see the exact terms. Returns {deleted: true}, or a not-found error when no such term is defined, so a second call fails rather than repeating. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: delete_glossary_term

tools.description: Permanently delete a recipe blueprint together with its recorded run history. Threads that earlier runs created are left alone, and a task schedule that pointed at the recipe stays and from then on fires a plain thread. Use list_recipes to find ids and instantiate_recipe to run a recipe instead of deleting it. Returns {deleted: true}, or a not-found error when the recipe does not exist or is in another workspace; you need access to the recipe's channel. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: delete_recipe

tools.description: Pause or resume a task schedule and return the updated schedule. A schedule fires only while active and past its next_run_at, so pausing stops its runs for everyone; resuming does not reset next_run_at. Setting the value it already has changes nothing but updated_at. Get schedule ids from list_task_schedules; to remove a schedule permanently use delete_task_schedule. Requires workspace:write and access to the schedule's channel.
tools.name: set_task_schedule_active

tools.description: Permanently delete a task schedule so it never fires again; use set_task_schedule_active to pause one you may want back. Threads the schedule already created are left alone. list_task_schedules finds schedule ids. Returns {deleted: true}, or a not-found error when the schedule does not exist; you need access to the schedule's channel. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: delete_task_schedule

tools.description: Revoke a slash command so it no longer runs: the command is disabled and stamped with revoked_at, its row is kept, and its name can be registered again. Returns the revoked command. An unknown or already revoked command is NotFound. Find command ids with list_slash_commands, and create commands with register_slash_command. Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: revoke_slash_command

tools.description: Revoke an FSM hook so it stops firing on thread state transitions. The hook is disabled and stamped with revoked_at rather than deleted, it no longer appears in list_fsm_hooks, and its in-memory signing secret is dropped. Revoking is final: a hook that is unknown, in another workspace or already revoked returns not found, so register a new one with register_fsm_hook to restore the behavior. Returns the revoked hook (id, label, from_state, to_state, handler_kind, handler_target, enabled, created_at, revoked_at). Requires workspace:write.
tools.name: revoke_fsm_hook

tools.description: Remove a thread's review requirement entirely, including its send-back cap, so the thread no longer needs any approval before it can close. This is a full waiver; to change how many approvals are needed use set_review_requirement (raising the count needs only thread:transition, lowering it channel:admin), and remove_reviewer takes a named reviewer off. Named reviewers stay, and the removal is recorded in the audit log as review_requirement.clear. Returns {cleared: true}, or a not-found error when the thread had no requirement. Requires channel:admin.
tools.name: clear_review_requirement

tools.description: Read the review requirement on a thread. NotFound when unset. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_review_requirement

tools.description: List the members named as reviewers on a thread, as a list of member ids, oldest designation first. An empty list means the review is open to any qualifying member. This is only the named set; for the approvals so far and whether the requirement is met use get_review_status, and for the recorded decisions use list_reviews. Names are added with add_reviewer and removed with remove_reviewer. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_reviewers

tools.description: Remove a member from a thread's named reviewer set and write a reviewer.remove audit record; it returns {removed: true}, or not found if the member was not named. This only edits who may be asked to review: it does not delete reviews already submitted. Add names with add_reviewer and read the set with list_reviewers. Requires channel:admin, which is stricter than the thread:transition that add_reviewer needs.
tools.name: remove_reviewer

tools.description: List the votes on a message, oldest first, as {message_id, member_id, kind, confidence, created_at} rows. kind is approve, request_changes or ack, and confidence is the voter's optional weight (by convention 0 to 1). Cast a vote with cast_vote and take one back with retract_vote; emoji reactions are separate and listed by list_reactions. Requires workspace:read and read access to the message.
tools.name: list_votes

tools.description: List the edit history of a message. A tombstoned message returns an empty list. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_message_edits

tools.description: Mark every notification for this member read. Same store path as POST /members/{id}/notifications/read-all, named beside mark_notification_read. Returns {cleared}. member_id must be the caller. Requires member:self.
tools.name: mark_all_notifications_read

tools.description: Ask a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, OpenAI's Decisions API, Google's Gemini Decisions API, Perplexity's Decisions API or Cloudflare's Clef) for advice on a task handed to review. Maidan sends the task's title, description and acceptance, its result and what the agent said, and returns ten yes/no judgments, each with a probability (does what the task asks, reports tests passing, the task asks for a code change, reports a failure, left work undone, asks a person, changes something not asked for, changes sign-in or permissions, deletes data, warns of a risk), plus land: green, amber or red by fixed rules. An unsettled judgment never counts toward green. Advice only: it does not write the gate, approve or close. NotFound when the instance offers no advice; the workspace needs a key for the provider asked unless the instance has one. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: advise_land_gate

tools.description: Store a named secret in the caller workspace. Returns metadata only; the plaintext is not echoed. Requires secret:admin.
tools.name: create_secret

tools.description: Delete a named secret in the caller workspace. Requires secret:admin.
tools.name: delete_secret

tools.description: Return artifact metadata and content_base64 bytes for a sha256 the caller workspace can access. A missing access ref is NotFound. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_artifact

tools.description: List the members of your own workspace, humans and agents, sorted by handle, as {id, workspace_id, handle, display_name, kind, created_at, updated_at, tombstoned_at}. kind is human or agent. The ids returned here are what member_id arguments elsewhere expect; use get_member for one member by id and whoami for your own identity. Same data as GET /workspaces/{wid}/members. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_members

tools.description: Fetch one member in the caller workspace. Another workspace is NotFound, same as an unknown id. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_member
